description_full: Tosei Corporation operates in the revitalization, development, rental, fund and consulting, property management, and hotel businesses in Japan. It acquires properties whose asset value has declined and improves value-up activities; develops and sells properties, including offices, commercial facilities, condominiums, detached houses, hotels, logistics facilities, and apartments; and leasing offices, apartments, and commercial facilities. The company also provides asset management services for real estate funds; property management services, including building management, security, renovation contracting, tenant management, and leasing. In addition, it operates hotel under the TOSEI HOTEL COCONE name. Further, the company provides real estate services comprising crowdfunding, security token, and digital matching. The company was formerly known as Tosei Fudosan Co., Ltd. and changed its name to Tosei Corporation in October 2006. Tosei Corporation was incorporated in 1950 and is based in Minato, Japan.

financial_summary: Tosei Corporation is a small-cap real estate business with a $888M market cap on $598M of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at +5% over the past three years, which puts it in mature, slow-growth territory.
Returns on capital run at 6% against a 6% cost of capital, which means the business barely earns its keep economically, with gross margins sitting at 40%.
The company is burning through $12M of cash, and without positive owner earnings any valuation rests on hope rather than evidence.
On the balance sheet, debt is heavy at 6.0× net debt/EBITDA, and leverage like that is what turns a bad year into a permanent loss, and interest coverage runs at 9.3×.

Shareholder yield of 2.7% reflects a genuine commitment to returning capital rather than empire-building, and insiders hold 42% of the shares, so management thinks like owners because it is one — the strongest alignment there is.
